# Raskell

> Writing about platform automation, edge systems, applied security, and open standards. Building automation-first platforms that survive production reality.

raskell.io is the personal site of Raffael Schneider, an AI Architect in Basel, Switzerland. He works on enterprise AI and agent platforms, edge infrastructure, applied security, and developer tooling, and writes long-form articles about them. Every article below links to a clean Markdown copy; the HTML page is the same URL without `.md`. Writing is licensed CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/) and code samples MIT: reuse, quote, and train on it with attribution, e.g. Raffael Schneider, "Article title", raskell.io, date, URL. Images, logos, and quoted third-party material are excluded (https://raskell.io/license/).

## Key pages

- [About](https://raskell.io/about/): who Raffael is, what he works on, and how to reach him
- [Start here](https://raskell.io/start-here/): curated reading tracks through the archive
- [Map](https://raskell.io/map/): every article, note, topic, series, and project as one graph; machine-readable at [map.json](https://raskell.io/map.json)
- [All writing in full](https://raskell.io/llms-full.txt): every article and note in one Markdown file, newest first
- [Notes](https://raskell.io/notes/): short notes that sit between the articles
- [RSS feed](https://raskell.io/rss.xml): full-text feed

## Series: The Agent Platform Handbook

1. [What an Agent Actually Is](https://raskell.io/articles/what-an-agent-actually-is.md): AI agent is the most overloaded word in the industry. This is the anatomy, the lineage, and a working implementation in roughly two hundred lines of TypeScript on Bun. Part one of The Agent Platform Handbook.
2. [Your Agent Wants Root](https://raskell.io/articles/your-agent-wants-root.md): An agent with a shell tool is arbitrary code execution with a friendly face. A short tour of why Docker alone is not enough, what Firecracker, gVisor, and Kata actually solve, and a hardened sandbox you can wrap the post-one agent in today. Part two of The Agent Platform Handbook.
3. [Tools: How Agents Actually Do Things](https://raskell.io/articles/tools-how-agents-actually-do-things.md): Function calling is the API between language and action, but the engineering is in the registry. A working four-tool registry in TypeScript on Bun, schema design that survives model drift, parallel tool calls, and the failure modes nobody mentions in the demo. Part three of The Agent Platform Handbook.
4. [Context Is the Product](https://raskell.io/articles/context-is-the-product.md): Models are commodities. Context is not. The sources of context an agent draws on, why retrieval alone is not enough, and a minimal .AGENTS/ convention that loads context from disk into the same harness we have been building. Part four of The Agent Platform Handbook.
5. [Retrieval Is a Tool, Not a Layer](https://raskell.io/articles/retrieval-is-a-tool-not-a-layer.md): Loading the whole .AGENTS/ directory on every turn does not scale. The fix is not a retrieval layer bolted to the side of the agent. It is a search tool in the registry the agent already has. BM25 over project docs, no vector store, and an honest account of when embeddings start to earn their keep. Part five of The Agent Platform Handbook.
6. [Memory Is a Write Path](https://raskell.io/articles/memory-is-a-write-path.md): Retrieval reads context the project authored. Memory is the agent writing context for its own future sessions, and the write is the part that is dangerous. Why session memory comes free from the transcript, why cross-session memory needs a separate write surface, and how to let an agent remember without letting it corrupt its own ground truth. Part six of The Agent Platform Handbook.
7. [The Model Is a Dependency](https://raskell.io/articles/the-model-is-a-dependency.md): Every layer of the harness has existed to put the right tokens in front of one hardcoded model string. This post pulls that string out and makes the model a dependency: why you route a cheap model for easy turns and a strong one for hard turns, what a fallback looks like when a provider is down, and why 'models are commodities' is a claim about your architecture before it is a claim about the market. Part seven of The Agent Platform Handbook.
8. [The Bill Is Part of the Loop](https://raskell.io/articles/the-bill-is-part-of-the-loop.md): Every model response already carries its own bill in the usage field, and the loop throws it away. This post reads that field, prices it against a table, and turns cost into a value the loop can see per turn and act on: a metering decorator that needs no loop change, a running ledger, prompt-cache accounting that moves the number the most, and a budget that degrades before it stops. Part eight of The Agent Platform Handbook.

## Articles

- [This Site Is Becoming a Map](https://raskell.io/articles/this-site-is-becoming-a-map.md) (2026-10-15): A blog shows what I wrote last. The new map on raskell.io shows what I keep coming back to, and it is the start of a public second brain.
- [The Bill Is Part of the Loop](https://raskell.io/articles/the-bill-is-part-of-the-loop.md) (2026-07-18): Every model response already carries its own bill in the usage field, and the loop throws it away. - [The Bottleneck Is Data, and Europe Is Sitting on It](https://raskell.io/articles/the-bottleneck-is-data-and-europe-is-sitting-on-it.md) (2026-06-30): Frontier AI is running short on public text, not compute. Europe's edge is the high-quality data it never put online. Capturing it needs coordination.
- [Brain Emulation, Read as an Infrastructure Problem](https://raskell.io/articles/brain-emulation-as-an-infrastructure-problem.md) (2026-06-28): An MIT thesis argues brain emulation has crossed into engineering. Read as infrastructure, the numbers describe a workload your AI cluster was not built for.
- [Memory Is a Write Path](https://raskell.io/articles/memory-is-a-write-path.md) (2026-06-23): Retrieval reads context the project authored. Part six of The Agent Platform Handbook.
- [The Proof You Only Have to Write Once](https://raskell.io/articles/the-proof-you-only-have-to-write-once.md) (2026-06-19): Generation is cheap, so verification is the bottleneck — and we throw the verification away every time. What if a proof, once written, could be named, shared, and vouched for? A content-addressed commons for verified Haskell, and the move I left for after the semantic-artifact trilogy.
- [Retrieval Is a Tool, Not a Layer](https://raskell.io/articles/retrieval-is-a-tool-not-a-layer.md) (2026-06-17): Loading the whole .AGENTS/ directory on every turn does not scale. Part four of The Agent Platform Handbook.

This is the anatomy, the lineage, and a working implementation in roughly two hundred lines of TypeScript on Bun. Part one of The Agent Platform Handbook.
- [The Field Exists Now](https://raskell.io/articles/the-field-exists-now.md) (2026-05-22): Alasdair Allan's agentlanguages.dev catalogue turns AI-oriented programming languages from a loose set of experiments into a field with camps, disagreements, and testable claims.
- [Source Code Is the New Assembly](https://raskell.io/articles/semantic-artifacts-and-meaning-engines.md) (2026-05-07): Closing the trilogy. The artifact you author is no longer source code. It is a typed, verifiable object that carries meaning. Code becomes a lowering target.
- [Patents Per Capita Is a Vanity Metric](https://raskell.io/articles/patents-per-capita-is-a-vanity-metric.md) (2026-05-01): Switzerland tops the Global Innovation Index for the fifteenth year running. As an engineer, that should make you suspicious of the metric, not proud of the country.
- [Traffic Replay as a Security Primitive](https://raskell.io/articles/traffic-replay-as-a-security-primitive.md) (2026-04-27): WAF tuning is a guessing game because you cannot reproduce the traffic that triggered the rule. Deterministic replay changes that.
- [The Economics of Inference](https://raskell.io/articles/the-economics-of-inference.md) (2026-04-22): Inference tokens are not API calls. They are a metered resource that is consumed, generates value, and correlates with power draw. The economics of the post-AI world look less like software and more like water, electricity, and gas.
- [What Comes After the Last Programming Language](https://raskell.io/articles/what-comes-after-the-last-programming-language.md) (2026-04-19): If AI generates machine code directly, why are we still running operating systems designed for humans? The answer might be an inference-native OS.
- [What Sixteen AI Agents Taught Me About Management](https://raskell.io/articles/what-sixteen-ai-agents-taught-me-about-management.md) (2026-04-16): What happens when you give sixteen AI agents an org chart, a reporting structure, and a token budget. A story about orchestration, management, and running out of runway.
- [Why We Built a Haskell Package Manager in Rust](https://raskell.io/articles/why-we-built-a-haskell-package-manager-in-rust.md) (2026-04-13): hx is a fast, opinionated Haskell toolchain built in Rust, following the playbook astral.sh used to modernize Python.
- [The Last Programming Language Might Not Be for Humans](https://raskell.io/articles/what-programming-languages-become-when-ai-writes-the-code.md) (2026-04-11): Three futures for programming languages as AI becomes the primary author of code, and why I bet on Haskell.
- [Notes from RSAC 2026](https://raskell.io/articles/notes-from-rsac-2026.md) (2026-04-09): Third time at RSA Conference, first time as a speaker. What I saw, what I heard, and what I am still processing.
- [What Zentinel Is Really Optimizing For](https://raskell.io/articles/what-zentinel-is-really-optimizing-for.md) (2026-03-22): Every major proxy was a product of its time. Zentinel is built for this one: safety, operability, and the operator's ability to sleep.
- [How I Work These Days](https://raskell.io/articles/how-i-work-these-days.md) (2026-03-15): From Kaggle in 2020 to coding agents in late 2025. The shift that changed how I build and why my routine finally feels right.
- [Archipelag.io Is in Open Beta: Here's Why I Built It](https://raskell.io/articles/archipelag-io-distributed-compute-from-mining-rigs-to-open-beta.md) (2026-03-13): From watching Ethereum miners in 2016 to building a decentralized compute network in open beta. Architecture, conviction, and the long road.
- [How AI Makes Bare Metal Viable Again](https://raskell.io/articles/how-ai-makes-bare-metal-viable-again.md) (2026-03-08): I migrated two production apps from Kubernetes to a single Hetzner box. The missing piece was not the hardware.
- [Edge Systems Are the New Backend](https://raskell.io/articles/edge-systems-are-the-new-backend.md) (2026-02-11): Auth, policy, and business logic are migrating to the edge. The traditional backend is becoming a persistence layer.
- [Looking back on 2025](https://raskell.io/articles/looking-back-on-2025.md) (2025-12-31): On reading Tim Berners-Lee in Okinawa, and why AI might accidentally save the web from itself.
- [Mise ate my Makefile](https://raskell.io/articles/mise-ate-my-makefile.md) (2025-12-14): Mise replaced Make, asdf, and a pile of shell scripts with a single TOML file per project. Here is why it stuck.
- [Disk space maintenance on Void Linux](https://raskell.io/articles/disk-space-void-linux-maintenance.md) (2024-05-01): Cleaning old kernels, pruning xbps package cache, and reclaiming disk space on Void Linux without breaking your system.
- [All beginning is Haskell](https://raskell.io/articles/all-beginning-is-haskell.md) (2023-03-06): How Haskell shaped the way I think about building systems, and why I am still building Haskell tooling years after writing my first monad.
- [My OpenBSD journey: Getting it virtualized with libvirt (1)](https://raskell.io/articles/my-openbsd-journey-getting-it-virtualized-with-libvirt-1.md) (2023-02-06): A step-by-step guide to running OpenBSD in a libvirt virtual machine on Void Linux, without needing VirtualBox or VMWare. Part 1 of my OpenBSD journey.
- [Hello and outlook](https://raskell.io/articles/hello-and-outlook.md) (2022-09-20): The first post on raskell.io. What this site is for and what I planned to write about.

## Topics

The topic vocabulary every page is filed under, with broader topics in brackets. Topic pages live at https://raskell.io/tags/<slug>/.

### Domains

- AI platforms (`ai-platforms`): The shared foundation an organisation builds AI on: model gateways, agent runtimes, governance, observability, and the operating model around them.
- AI-assisted engineering (`ai-engineering`): AI as an engineering tool: coding agents, AI-authored code, and what programming becomes when models write most of it.
- AI for operations (`ai-for-ops`): AI applied to running systems: security triage, alert noise, incident work, and keeping a human in the loop.
- Platform automation (`platform-automation`): Self-service, guardrails, deployment, and the tooling that keeps operating software sustainable.
- Edge systems (`edge-systems`): Reverse proxies, policy enforcement, CDNs, and logic that runs close to the user instead of in the backend.
- Applied security (`applied-security`): Security under production pressure: adversarial input, signal versus noise, and controls that operators can live with.
- Distributed systems (`distributed-systems`): Replication, coordination, and consistency across machines that fail independently.
- Programming languages (`programming-languages`): Languages, type systems, compilers, and how executable intent gets written down.
- Operating systems (`operating-systems`): Kernels, virtualisation, and the layer between hardware and everything else, from BSD to inference-native designs.
- Reliability (`reliability`): Failure modes, operability, and keeping systems up when the inputs and the dependencies misbehave.
- Sovereignty (`sovereignty`): Who controls compute, data, and infrastructure, and in which jurisdiction; Europe's position in particular.
- Policy (`policy`): Where engineering meets regulation, public institutions, procurement, and national strategy.
- The open web (`open-web`): The web as a commons: open protocols, small independent sites, and publishing outside the platforms.

### Concepts

- Agents (`agents`) [within AI platforms]: LLM agents as software: the loop, tools, context, memory, sandboxes, and the platform underneath them.
- Context engineering (`context-engineering`) [within Agents]: Deciding what a model sees: pinned context, retrieval, memory, and the conventions that keep them honest.
- Inference (`inference`) [within AI platforms]: Running models in production: routing, cost, hardware, and inference as a metered utility.
- Isolation (`isolation`) [within Applied security, Reliability]: Sandboxes, process and failure-domain isolation, and running untrusted or fallible work safely.
- WAF and traffic inspection (`waf`) [within Applied security, Edge systems]: Web application firewalls, rule tuning, traffic replay, and inspecting requests without drowning operators.
- Observability (`observability`) [within Reliability]: Seeing what a running system does: traces, metering, glass-box infrastructure, and what not to log.
- Economics (`economics`): Cost, pricing, budgets, and the money side of infrastructure, inference, and innovation.
- Metrics (`metrics`): What to measure, leading versus lagging signals, and vanity numbers that look like insight.
- Formal methods (`formal-methods`) [within Programming languages]: Proofs, verification, and types as specifications, especially once machines write the code.
- Developer tooling (`developer-tooling`) [within Platform automation]: Package managers, build tools, CLIs, and the daily toolchain an engineer actually touches.
- Self-hosting (`self-hosting`) [within Platform automation, Sovereignty]: Running your own infrastructure, from a single bare-metal box to community-operated compute.
- Complex systems (`complex-systems`): Emergence and collective dynamics: how simple agents, roles, and rules add up to markets, institutions, and societies.
- Local-first (`local-first`) [within Distributed systems]: Software that keeps data on your devices and syncs through CRDTs, with the network as an optimisation.
- Knowledge management (`knowledge-management`): Second brains, knowledge graphs, and how notes, links, and memory turn into understanding.
- Open source (`oss`) [within The open web]: Open source and open standards as the point of the work, not just its licence.

### Technologies

- Rust (`rust`) [within Programming languages]: The systems language most of the projects here are written in.
- Haskell (`haskell`) [within Programming languages]: The language that shaped how I think about types, effects, and correctness.
- TypeScript (`typescript`) [within Programming languages]: TypeScript on Bun, the language of the Agent Platform Handbook code.
- Elixir (`elixir`) [within Programming languages]: Elixir, Phoenix, and the BEAM for the long-running, fault-tolerant parts.
- Pingora (`pingora`) [within Edge systems, Rust]: Cloudflare's Rust framework for building proxies, the base of Zentinel.
- Kubernetes (`kubernetes`) [within Platform automation]: Container orchestration, and the question of when you actually need it.
- GPUs (`gpus`) [within Inference]: GPUs as the computer: memory shape, partitioning, and the hardware under inference.
- Linux (`linux`) [within Operating systems]: Linux distributions and system administration, Void Linux in particular.
- OpenBSD (`openbsd`) [within Operating systems]: OpenBSD and the BSD approach to correctness and simplicity.
- Zola (`zola`) [within The open web]: The static site generator this site and several project sites are built with.

### This site

- This site (`meta`): Posts about raskell.io itself: why it exists, how it is built, and where it is going.

## Projects

- [Archipelag.io](https://archipelag.io): Decentralized AI compute platform.
- [Cyanea](https://cyanea.bio): The open community for life science research.
- [Humankind.](https://humankind.plus): Human continuity platform for preserving presence across generations.
- [Arcanist](https://arcanist.sh): High-performance Haskell tooling, built in Rust.
- [Zentinel](https://zentinelproxy.io): Guardian of the Free Web.
- [broodwar.live](https://broodwar.live): The community platform for StarCraft: Brood War competitive play, a basketball-reference.com for Brood War.
- [Conflux](https://github.com/raskell-io/conflux): Schema-aware config state coordination.
- [hx](https://hx.arcanist.sh): An extremely fast Haskell package and project manager, written in Rust.
- [bhc](https://bhc.arcanist.sh): The Basel Haskell Compiler.
- [Shiioo (CO)](https://github.com/raskell-io/shiioo): The Virtual Company OS.
- [Sango](https://sango.raskell.io): Edge diagnostics for the modern web.
- [Ushio](https://github.com/raskell-io/ushio): Deterministic edge traffic replay for understanding WAF and proxy behavior.
- [Vela](https://github.com/raskell-io/vela): No-downtime app deployment on bare metal.
- [Refrakt](https://github.com/raskell-io/refrakt): A convention-first web framework for Gleam.
- [Die Zukunft](https://die-zukunft.ch): A Swiss movement that applies engineering principles to public life: not left, not right.
- [Human Macroscope](https://github.com/human-macroscope): A long-term interdisciplinary research project on humans and human collectives across scales, from individuals and families to institutions, cultures, and civilizations: how individual traits, roles, relations, and cultural transmission combine into emergent collective properties.
- [coconutOS](https://github.com/coconut-os/coconutOS): A Rust microkernel for GPU-isolated AI inference.
- [Driftscape](https://github.com/raskell-io/driftscape): Ambient soundscape platform.
- [robogym](https://github.com/raskell-io/robogym): Rust/Bevy PWA for training robotic agents.
- [Awesomeify](https://github.com/raskell-io/awesomeify): Index GitHub repos and generate static awesome-list sites.
- [Learn You the Web](https://learn-you-the-web.raskell.io): A friendly guide to how the web actually works.

## Apps

- [Manabi](https://manabi.raskell.io): A reading-first language-learning app for Chinese, Japanese, Korean, and Hebrew.
- [Kurumi](https://kurumi.raskell.io): A local-first, AI-native second brain.
- [Paw & Claw](https://pawandclaw.raskell.io): A turn-based strategy game in the spirit of Advance Wars, fought by woodland armies.
- [Terrarium](https://github.com/raskell-io/terrarium): A societal simulation engine where LLM-powered agents form emergent civilizations.

## For agents

- Each article and note as Markdown: its URL with `.md` instead of the trailing slash, e.g. https://raskell.io/articles/the-model-is-a-dependency.md
- [map.json](https://raskell.io/map.json): the site graph (pages, topics with definitions, series, projects, and their links)
- [api-catalog](https://raskell.io/.well-known/api-catalog): RFC 9727 discovery of the machine-readable files
- Feeds: [RSS](https://raskell.io/rss.xml), [Atom](https://raskell.io/atom.xml), [articles](https://raskell.io/articles/rss.xml), [notes](https://raskell.io/notes/rss.xml)
- In the browser: WebMCP tools (search_site, get_current_page, get_page_markdown, get_site_index, list_topics, get_connections, cite_current_page, open_page) register when an agent exposes `document.modelContext`.
- No authentication, no rate limits ([auth.md](https://raskell.io/.well-known/auth.md)). Crawling for search, answers, and training is welcome (robots.txt Content-Signal).
